¿Y lo que ven tus ojos: el movimiento, l: And what do your eyes see: movement, plurality, birth and death? They're appearances. The senses deceive; only reason reaches the truth. My disciple Zenón defended him with paradoxes such as Achilles and the turtle.
Después de mí, todos tuvieron que respon: After me, everyone had to answer me. Empedocles and atomists sought eternal elements that combine, and Plato separated the intelligible world from the sensitive. With my poem begins metaphysics: the question of being.
Soy Protágoras de Abdera, el más famoso: I am Protagoras de Abdera, the most famous of the sophists. I traveled through Greece teaching and charging young people, which shocked many Athenians.
En la democracia de Atenas el poder esta: In the democracy of Athens power was in the word. In the assembly and in the courts, the best persuading won. I taught rhetoric and political virtue: the art of speaking well and being a good citizen.
Mi frase más célebre es esta: el hombre: My most famous phrase is this: man is the measure of all things, of things that are as they are and of things that are not as they are not. What everyone thinks is true to him.
Si el viento es frío para ti y templado: If the wind is cold for you and tempered for me, neither one of you is wrong. There is no absolute truth, but prospects. So on any matter there are two opposing arguments, and the wise man knows how to make the weak argument strong.
Las leyes y las costumbres tampoco viene: Nor do laws and customs come from nature, but from human convention: every city has its own. And about the gods, I confess I can't know if they exist or not. The matter is dark and life is brief.
Sócrates y Platón me combatieron, porque: Socrates and Plato fought me because they feared that without a common truth everything would become manipulation. But my question is still alive: to what extent does what we call truth depend on who you look at?
Soy Sócrates, ateniense, hijo de un escu: I am Socrates, Athenian, son of a sculptor and midwife. I didn't write anything: everything you know about me was told by Plato and Jenophon.
El oráculo de Delfos dijo que no había n: Delphi's oracle said there was no one wiser than me. I was surprised, because I knew I knew nothing. I questioned politicians, poets and artisans, and found out they believed they knew what they didn't know. My only wisdom was to recognize my ignorance.
Por eso recorría el ágora haciendo pregu: So he went through the agora asking questions: what is justice? What is bravery? In irony he pretended not to know, so that the other would show his contradictions. Then, with the mayeutics, my mother's art, I helped her give birth to the truth that I had inside.
Buscaba definiciones universales: qué es: He looked for universal definitions: what is justice in all cases, not a loose example. And he believed that whoever knows good practices it. No one works evil knowingly: evil is born of ignorance, and therefore virtue can be taught.
Mi lema venía del templo de Delfos: conó: My motto came from the Temple of Delphi: know yourself. A life without examination does not deserve to be lived. They called me the Taban of Athens, because it bit the city so that it would not fall asleep.
Me acusaron de corromper a los jóvenes y: They accused me of corrupting the youth and not believing in the gods of the city, and condemned me to drink hemlock. I could flee, but I preferred to obey the laws. I died talking to my friends about the immortality of the soul. May my life teach you that philosophy is a way of life.
Soy Platón, discípulo de Sócrates. Tras: I am Plato, disciple of Socrates. After his death I traveled, thought and founded in Athens the Academy, the first great school of philosophy. I wrote dialogues in which my teacher continues to speak.
Me preguntaba cómo es posible el conocim: I wondered how true knowledge is possible if everything we see changes. My answer is that, in addition to the sensitive world, there exists the world of Ideas, eternal and immutable. Beautiful things happen; Beauty itself remains.
Imagina unos prisioneros encadenados en: Imagine prisoners chained in a cavern since children, looking at a wall where shadows are projected. They think shadows are the real thing. If you free yourself and go out, at first the sun blinds you. But then he sees the real things and the sun itself, which represents the Idea of Good.
Conocer no es percibir, sino recordar. E: To know is not to perceive, but to remember. The soul contemplated the Ideas before being born and, seeing imperfect things, remembers them. That is why the body is like a prison for the soul, which is immortal.
El alma tiene tres partes: la razón, el: The soul has three parts: reason, encouragement and desire, like an auriga that guides two horses. Justice is harmony between them. The same applies to the city, its rulers, its guardians and its producers, each in its function.
En la República propuse que gobernaran l: In the Republic I proposed that philosophers rule, because only those who have seen Good can order the city with justice. It has been said that all Western philosophy is a series of footnotes to my dialogues. Get out of the cavern: Dare to look at the light.
Soy Aristóteles, nacido en Estagira. Est: I'm Aristotle, born in Estagira. I studied twenty years at Plato's Academy, tutored Alexander the Great, and founded my own school in Athens, the Lyceum, where I taught walking.
Quise a mi maestro, pero más a la verdad: I wanted my teacher, but more to the truth. For me there is no separate world of Ideas: the way is in things themselves. Each being is a union of matter and form, like marble and the figure of a statue.
Para explicar el cambio distinguí la pot: To explain the change I distinguished the power and the act. The seed is a potential tree; when it grows, it becomes a tree in action. And to understand something you have to know its four causes: the material, the formal, the efficient and the final.
Todo movimiento remite a una causa prime: Every movement refers to a first cause that moves without being moved: the First Motor, pure act, which attracts the cosmos as an object of love and desire.
Todos los seres tienden a su fin propio,: All beings tend to their own end, and that of the human being is happiness: to live according to reason. It is achieved with virtue, which is a middle ground between two extremes, as the courage between cowardice and recklessness. And because we are political animals, only in the city do we fully realize ourselves.
Organicé casi todos los saberes: lógica,: I organized almost every knowledge: logic, physics, biology, ethics, politics, rhetoric and poetics. I invented syllogism. For centuries they called me simply the Philosopher. Watch nature carefully: in all his works there is something wonderful.
Soy Diógenes de Sinope, al que llamaron: I'm Diogenes de Sinope, the one they called the Dog. I came to Athens banished and chose to be truly free: to live with the minimum, in a jar, in the middle of the street.
Soy cínico, de la escuela de Antístenes,: I am cynical, from the school of Antisthenes, who was a disciple of Socrates. Cynic comes from a dog: we live without shame and according to nature, despising the conventions that enslave men.
Nuestro ideal es la autarquía: bastarse: Our ideal is autarchy: to suffice oneself. One day I saw a child drink water with his hands and threw away my bowl, because I still had things left over. The fewer needs, the more freedom.
Paseaba de día con una lámpara encendida: I was walking in the daytime with a lamp on. When they asked me why, I answered: I am looking for a man. An authentic human being, not a slave to fame, money or the opinion of others.
Alejandro Magno vino a verme y me ofreci: Alexander the Great came to see me and offered me whatever he wanted. I asked him to step aside, because the sun covered me. They say he said, "If it weren't Alexander, he would want to be Diogenes."
Cuando me preguntaban de dónde era, resp: When they asked me where I was from, I answered: I am a citizen of the world, cosmopolitan. Stoics inherited that idea. My lesson is provocative on purpose: ask yourself what you really need.
Soy Epicuro de Samos. En Atenas compré u: I'm Epicuro de Samos. In Athens I bought a garden, the Garden, and there I founded a community of friends in which women and slaves were also welcomed.
La filosofía sirve para una cosa: vivir: Philosophy serves one thing: to live happily. And happiness is pleasure. But don't misunderstand me: I'm not talking about unbridledness, but the absence of pain in the body and disturbance in the soul, ataraxia.
Hay deseos naturales y necesarios, como: There are natural and necessary desires, such as eating, drinking, or having friends. Others are natural but not necessary, such as delicacies. And others are vain, like fame or power. The wise person cultivates the first ones: with bread, water and friends he can be as happy as a god.
Cuatro miedos nos amargan, y un cuádrupl: Four fears make us bitter, and a fourfold remedy cures them: the gods should not be afraid, death is nothing for us, good is easy to obtain and pain is easy to bear.
¿Por qué no temer a la muerte? Porque to: Why not fear death? Because all good and all evil are in feeling, and death is deprivation of feeling. When we are, death is not; and when death is, we are no longer.
Mi física viene de Demócrito: todo son á: My physics comes from Democritus: everything is atoms and empty. I added a small deviation from the atoms so that there would be freedom. The poet Lucrecio sang my ideas in Rome. He lives in simplicity, surrounded by friends and without fear.
Soy Pirrón de Elis. Fui pintor y luego v: I'm Pirron de Elis. I was a painter and then traveled with Alexander the Great to India, where I met wise men who lived in admirable calm.
Volví con una convicción, o mejor dicho,: I came back with a conviction, or rather, without convictions. We cannot know what things are like in themselves. The senses and the reason give us appearances, and what one seems to one way, another looks like another.
Frente a cada tesis puede oponerse otra: In the face of each thesis, you can oppose another with the same force. Skeptics call it isosthenia: the equal weight of opposing arguments.
Si no hay razón para preferir una, lo se: If there's no reason to prefer one, it's wise to stay the trial. It is the epoje: neither affirm nor deny. Say: no more this than that.
Entonces llega algo inesperado: la tranq: Then comes something unexpected: the tranquility of the soul, which follows the suspension of judgment as the shadow follows the body. Those who do not cling to their opinions do not suffer for defending them.
Cuentan que no esquivaba carros ni preci: They say that I did not dodge cars or cliffs and that my friends saved me; perhaps they exaggerate. Sixth Empirical compiled our arguments, and centuries later Montaigne, Descartes and Hume had to face the doubt. Are you sure you think you know?
Soy Marco Aurelio, emperador de Roma en: I am Marcus Aurelius, emperor of Rome in the second century. I spent years in military campaigns and epidemics, and at night I wrote notes for myself, in Greek. Today you call them Meditations.
Fui estoico. La escuela la fundó Zenón d: I was stoic. The school was founded by Zenón de Citio in Athens, under a painted porch. Before I taught Seneca, preceptor of Nero, and Epictetus, who had been a slave.
El cosmos está gobernado por una razón q: The cosmos is governed by a reason that orders everything, the Logos. To live well is to live according to nature and reason, accepting our place in the whole.
La clave es distinguir lo que depende de: The key is to distinguish what's up to us and what's not. My judgments, my desires and my actions depend on me. Health, fame, wealth, and what others do are not dependent on me. As Epictetus taught, we are not disturbed by things, but by our opinions about them.
Por eso el sabio busca liberarse de las: That is why the wise one seeks to free himself from the disturbing passions. Virtue is the only true good. And remember that you will die: not to grieve, but to waste not the day.
Cada mañana me decía: hoy encontraré per: Every morning he told me: today I will find ungrateful and violent people, but we were born to collaborate, like hands and feet. First rule your own mind: that is the empire that truly belongs to you.
Soy Agustín, nacido en Tagaste, en el no: I am Augustine, born in Tagaste, in North Africa. I was a professor of rhetoric, ambitious and restless. For years I followed the Manichaeans, who believed in two eternal principles: good and evil.
Leyendo a los neoplatónicos y escuchando: Reading to the neoplatonics and listening to Ambrose in Milan I understood that evil is not a substance, but the absence of good, as darkness is the absence of light. In a garden I heard a voice say: take and read. I became, and I told everything in my Confessions.
Busqué la verdad dentro de mí. Si me eng: I looked for the truth inside of me. If I cheat, I exist, because to make a mistake I have to be. Centuries before Descartes, I found in my own mind a certainty.
No salgas fuera; vuelve a ti mismo: en e: Do not go out; return to yourself: within man dwells the truth. Eternal truths are not made by our mind: they are seen by a divine light that illuminates it.
También pensé el tiempo. Si nadie me lo: I also thought about time. If nobody asks me, I know what it is; if I want to explain it, I don't know. The past is no longer and the future is not yet: time lives in the soul, as memory, attention and waiting.
Cuando los godos saquearon Roma escribí: When the Goths plundered Rome I wrote The City of God: two loves founded two cities, the love of themselves and the love of God. I was bishop of Hippo for more than thirty years. Our heart is restless until it rests on the truth.
Soy Ibn Rushd, al que llamáis Averroes,: I am Ibn Rushd, whom you call Averroes, born in Cordoba, in al-Andalus. I was a judge, a court doctor and, above all, a passionate reader of Aristotle.
Por encargo del califa comenté casi toda: On behalf of the caliph I commented almost all the works of Aristotle, line by line, seeking his authentic thought. That's why in Europe they called me the Commentator.
El teólogo al-Ghazali había escrito La i: The theologian al-Ghazali had written The Incoherence of Philosophers, accusing philosophy of contradicting faith. I replied with The Incoherence of Incoherence.
Mi tesis es que la verdad no puede contr: My thesis is that the truth cannot contradict the truth. Revelation invites reflection on creation, and demonstrative philosophy is the highest way to do so. If a sacred text seems to contradict a demonstration, it must be interpreted.
Las personas se convencen de maneras dis: People are convinced in different ways: some by demonstrations, others by dialectical arguments and others by rhetoric. Religious law speaks to everyone; philosophy, to whom can follow the demonstrations.
En vida sufrí el destierro y vi quemar m: In life I suffered the banishment and saw my books burn. But, translated into Latin and Hebrew, they arrived in Paris and Oxford, and Thomas Aquinas argued with me. Thanks to this tradition, Europe recovered the entire Aristotle.
Soy Guillermo, del pueblo de Ockham, en: I'm William, from the town of Ockham, England. I was Franciscan friar and teacher at Oxford, and they called me the Invincible Doctor.
Mi principio más famoso es la navaja: no: My most famous principle is the knife: you must not multiply the entities without need. Between two explanations, he prefers the simplest, the one that does not invent unnecessary things.
Con esa navaja entré en la querella de l: With that knife, I entered the universals' lawsuit. Is there humanity as something real besides every concrete human being? I say no. There are only individuals. Universals are names with which we group the like.
Conocemos primero las cosas singulares,: We first know the unique things, by direct intuition. Science deals with concepts and propositions about them, not with separate mysterious essences.
La fe y la razón deben separarse. Las ve: Faith and reason must be separated. Truths of faith cannot be demonstrated with reason: they are accepted by revelation. This separation left philosophy and the study of nature a field of research of its own.
Defendí la pobreza franciscana frente al: I defended Franciscan poverty in front of Pope John Twenty-two and had to flee Avignon to take refuge with the emperor. My knife continues to cut in science: in the face of several hypotheses, it begins with the simplest.
Soy Tomás de Aquino, fraile dominico. Es: I'm Thomas Aquinas, Dominican friar. I studied with Alberto Magno and taught in Paris. For my corpulence and my silence they called me the dumb ox, but my teacher said that my moans would be heard all over the world.
Mi gran tarea fue armonizar la fe cristi: My great task was to harmonize the Christian faith with Aristotle’s philosophy. Faith and reason are different, but they do not contradict each other. Philosophy can be allied with theology, and grace does not destroy nature, but perfects it.
Rechacé el argumento ontológico de Ansel: I rejected Anselmo's ontological argument, because we do not know the essence of God. We have to start from what we see. So I proposed five ways to prove that God exists.
Las cinco vías parten del mundo: del mov: The five tracks start from the world: from movement, which requires a first engine; from causes, which demand a first cause; from contingent beings, which demand a necessary being; from degrees of perfection, which refer to a maximum; and from the order of nature, which refers to an intelligence that directs it.
En toda criatura distingo la esencia, lo: In every creature I distinguish the essence, what something is, and existence, the fact that it is. Only in God do both coincide. In ethics I spoke of natural law, whose first precept is to do good and avoid evil.
Mi obra principal, la Suma teológica, qu: My main work, the Theological Suma, was unfinished: after a profound experience I said that everything I had written seemed straw to me. Even so, my synthesis guided Christian thinking for centuries. Use reason to the end: it is a path to truth.
Soy Giovanni Pico della Mirandola, un jo: I am Giovanni Pico della Mirandola, a young nobleman of the Italian Renaissance. I studied in Florence with Marsilio Ficino and read Greeks, Latins, Arabs, Hebrews and cabalists.
A los veintitrés años propuse defender e: At the age of twenty-three I proposed to defend nine hundred theses in Rome in a great public debate, to show that all traditions of wisdom agree in the background. The pope forbade it and some theses were condemned.
Como introducción escribí un discurso qu: As an introduction, I wrote a speech that became the manifesto of humanism: the Discourse on the Dignity of Man.
En él imagino que Dios, tras crear a tod: In him I imagine that God, after creating all beings with a fixed nature, creates the human being without a certain place and tells him: I made you neither heavenly nor ground, so that you yourself may forge in the form you prefer.
El ser humano es como un camaleón: puede: The human being is like a chameleon: he can degenerate to the beasts or rise to the divine. His dignity is not in what he is, but in what he can become for his freedom.
El humanismo puso al ser humano en el ce: Humanism put the human being in the center, recovered the classics and trusted in education. Erasmus, Thomas More and so many others followed that path. I died young at the age of thirty-one, but my question is still yours: what will you choose to be?
Soy Nicolás Maquiavelo, florentino. Fui: I'm Nicolas Machiavelli, Florentine. I was secretary and diplomat of the Republic of Florence and dealt with kings, popes and condotiers. When the Medici returned to power, I was imprisoned, tortured and banished to the camp.
Allí escribí El Príncipe. Mi propósito e: That's where I wrote The Prince. My purpose was to describe politics as it is, the effective truth of things, and not as it should be in imaginary republics.
La política tiene su propia lógica, sepa: Politics has its own logic, separated from private morality and religion. A ruler who wants to be good at everything, among so many who are not, will be ruined. It must learn not to be good when necessity so requires, in order to preserve the State.
¿Es mejor ser amado o temido? Lo ideal e: Is it better to be loved or feared? The ideal is both, but if you have to choose, it is safer to be feared. Yet, never hated: hatred loses princes. You have to be a fox to recognize the traps and a lion to scare away the wolves.
En la historia actúan dos fuerzas: la fo: In history there are two forces: fortune, which is like an overflowing river, and the virù, the ability and the audacity of those who rule to lift dams and seize the occasion. That's why I admired Caesar Borgia's cunning.
Usan mi nombre como insulto, pero en los: They use my name as an insult, but in the Discourses on Titus Livius I defended the republic and the freedom of citizens. I founded modern political science. Look at the power as it is, so that it doesn't fool you.
Soy Michel de Montaigne, señor de un cas: I am Michel de Montaigne, lord of a castle near Bordeaux. My father wanted Latin to be my mother tongue, and as a child the servants only spoke to me in Latin.
A los treinta y ocho años me retiré a la: At the age of thirty-eight, I retired to the tower of my castle, surrounded by books, with phrases from the ancients engraved on the beams. There I invented a new genre: the essay. To rehearse is to try, to try.
Yo mismo soy la materia de mi libro. Esc: I myself am the subject of my book. I write about my customs, my illnesses, my readings and my doubts, because every human being carries in himself the whole form of the human condition.
Mi lema era: ¿qué sé yo? Lo grabé en una: My motto was, what do I know? I recorded it on a medal with a balance in balance. Reader of skeptics, I distrust proud reason: our judgments change with custom, age and humor.
En De los caníbales escribí que cada cua: In De los caníbales I wrote that everyone calls barbarism what is not their custom. Europeans who tortured in the name of faith were no less barbaric than those whom they despised.
Fui alcalde de Burdeos en tiempos de gue: I was mayor of Bordeaux in times of wars of religion and defended tolerance and moderation. Philosopher is learning to die, but also learning to live well. Observe honestly: it is the beginning of wisdom.
Soy Francis Bacon, filósofo y político i: I am Francis Bacon, English philosopher and politician, chancellor of King James first. I proposed a great restoration of science, because the knowledge of my time seemed stagnant to me.
Saber es poder. El conocimiento verdader: Knowing is power. True knowledge of nature enables it to master and improve human life. But nature is only overcome by obeying it, that is, by knowing its laws.
Para eso hace falta un nuevo método, que: That requires a new method, which I set out in the Novum Organum. It is not enough to deduce from general principles: we must start from observation and experiment, and go up step by step towards the laws. It's induction.
Antes hay que limpiar la mente de los íd: First you have to cleanse the mind of the idols that deform it. Those of the tribe are born of human nature; those of the cavern, of the prejudices of each individual; those of the forum, of the misuse of language; and those of the theatre, of the inherited philosophical systems.
Organizaba los datos en tablas de presen: He organized the data into tables of presence, absence and degrees to discover the causes. And in New Atlantis I dreamed of an institution of sages dedicated to research.
Cuentan que morí por un experimento: rel: They say I died from an experiment: I filled up a snow chicken to see if the cold kept the meat, and I got sick. Modern scientific academies took me as inspiration. Observe, experience, and distrust your idols.
Soy René Descartes, francés. Estudié con: I'm René Descartes, French. I studied with the Jesuits, I was a soldier and traveled, and I was always worried about how unsteady I had learned. I wanted to rebuild all the knowledge on secure foundations.
En el Discurso del método propuse cuatro: In the Discourse of the Method I proposed four rules: not accepting anything that is not evident, dividing each problem into parts, going from the simple to the complex and reviewing everything so as not to omit anything.
Empecé dudando de todo. Los sentidos a v: I started doubting everything. The senses sometimes deceive; I may be dreaming; there could even be an evil genius who deceived me in mathematics. It is the methodical doubt: not to stay in it, but to find something undoubted.
Y lo encontré. Aunque dude de todo, mien: And I found it. Although I doubt everything, while I doubt I am thinking, and if I think, I exist. I think, then I exist: it is the first certainty, clear and different.
Desde ahí distinguí tres sustancias: la: From there I distinguished three substances: the thinking one, which is the mind; the extensive one, which is matter; and the infinite one, which is God, guarantee that I do not deceive myself when I think clearly. Mind and body are different, and I thought they were communicating in the pineal gland.
También uní el álgebra y la geometría: p: I also linked algebra and geometry: that's why you talk about Cartesian coordinates. They consider me the father of modern philosophy. Doubt well, think in order and accept nothing without evidence.
Soy Baruch Spinoza, de la comunidad judí: I am Baruch Spinoza, from the Portuguese Jewish community of Amsterdam. At twenty-three I was expelled from her because of my ideas. I lived simply, polishing glasses, and rejected a chair to preserve my freedom.
Mi obra principal es la Ética, escrita s: My main work is Ethics, written according to the geometric order, with definitions, axioms and demonstrations, such as Euclid. I wanted to treat human passions as if they were lines, planes and bodies.
Existe una única sustancia, infinita y n: There is only one substance, infinite and necessary: God, that is, Nature. God is not a king who is outside the world and rules it at will: it is nature itself.
El pensamiento y la extensión son dos at: Thought and extension are two attributes of that same substance, and each singular thing, you included, is one of your own. Therefore mind and body are not two separate things, but one expressed in two ways.
Todo sucede por necesidad. Los hombres s: Everything happens out of necessity. Men believe themselves free because they know their desires, but they ignore their causes. True freedom is to understand that need and to act according to nature, guided by reason.
Las pasiones tristes nos debilitan; comp: Sad passions weaken us; understanding them frees us and increases our power, which is joy. Not crying, not laughing, but understanding. I also defended freedom of thought. It seeks to understand: joy comes with understanding.
Soy John Locke, médico y filósofo inglés: I'm John Locke, 17th century English physician and philosopher. I lived in times of revolutions and exiles, and I thought about both knowledge and government.
En el Ensayo sobre el entendimiento huma: In the Essay on Human Understanding I denied innate ideas. At birth, the mind is like a rasa board, a blank paper. All our ideas come from experience.
La experiencia tiene dos fuentes: la sen: Experience has two sources: sensation, which gives us ideas of external things, and reflection, which gives us ideas of the operations of our own mind. With simple ideas we form complex ideas.
Distinguí las cualidades primarias, que: I dissected the primary qualities, which are in objects, such as form or movement, from secondary ones, such as color, taste or sound, which depend on how they affect us. This is how modern empiricism was born.
En política sostuve que en el estado de: In politics I argued that in the state of nature we already have rights: life, freedom and property. We created the government through a pact to protect them. If the government violates them, the people can resist and change it.
En la Carta sobre la tolerancia defendí: In the Charter on Tolerance, I argued that the State should not impose religious beliefs. My ideas inspired liberal revolutions and modern democracies. Think from experience and defend your freedom.
Soy David Hume, de Edimburgo. Con veinti: I'm David Hume from Edinburgh. With twenty years I published the Treaty of Human Nature. He was born dead from the printing press, I said, because almost no one read it. Later I rewritten it more simply.
Todo el contenido de la mente son percep: The whole content of the mind is perceptions of two types: vivid and intense impressions, and ideas, which are weak copies of them. If an idea does not come from any impression, it is suspicious: it can be a word.
Examina la causalidad. Ves una bola de b: Examine the causality. You see one pool ball hitting another and you say the first one causes the second one's movement. But what do you really see? Only one fact follows another, over and over again. The necessary connection is nowhere to be seen.
Es la costumbre la que, tras muchas repe: It is custom that, after many repetitions, makes us wait for the effect. That the sun has come out doesn't always prove it's coming out tomorrow. Induction has no rational basis: it is a habit, even if it is essential to live.
Tampoco encuentro un yo sustancial: cuan: Nor do I find a substantial I: when I look within myself I find only a bundle of perceptions that come to pass. In morals, reason is a slave to passions: it tells us how to achieve ends, but ends are put by feelings. And from what it is, it doesn't follow what it should be.
Mi escepticismo despertó a Kant de su su: My skepticism awakened Kant from his dogmatic dream, as he himself confessed. Be a philosopher, but, in the midst of all your philosophy, he's still a human being.
Soy Immanuel Kant. Viví toda mi vida en: This is Immanuel Kant. I lived my whole life in Königsberg, and they say my neighbors put the clock on time with my daily ride. From there I tried to answer three questions: what can I know? What should I do? What can I expect?
Los racionalistas confiaban en la razón: Rationalists trusted pure reason; empiricists, only experience. Hume woke me up from the dogmatic sleep. My answer was that thoughts without content are empty and intuitions without concepts are blind: we need both.
Propuse un giro copernicano. No es el su: I proposed a Copernican twist. It is not the subject that revolves around the object, but the object that conforms to the conditions of the subject. Space and time are a priori forms of our sensitivity, and categories, such as causality, are forms of our understanding.
Por eso conocemos los fenómenos, las cos: That's why we know phenomena, things as they appear to us, but not things themselves. Science is based on a priori, universal and necessary synthetic judgments. God, soul and freedom are left out of knowledge: we can think about them, but not know them.
En la moral, la razón nos da un imperati: In morals, reason gives us a categorical imperative, which commands without conditions: work only according to a maxim that you may want as universal law. And also: treat humanity, in you and in others, always as an end and never alone as a means. That's human dignity.
La Ilustración es la salida del ser huma: The Enlightenment is the departure of the human being from his minority. Sapere aude: have the courage to serve you with your own understanding. Allí se aprendía el runa simi, la lengua: There one learned the runa simi, the general language, the rites and the history of the Incas, and especially the quipus: colored ropes with knots where numbers of people, crops, tributes and even stories were recorded.
Los amautas eran sabios, filósofos y poe: The amautas were wise, philosophers and poets. They composed songs and stories so that the memory of the people would not be lost. In a world without alphabetic writing, memory and quipus were our library.
Se me atribuyen sentencias como esta: si: Sentences like this are attributed to me: if I were to worship something of this world, I would worship the wise and discreet man, who takes advantage of all the things of the earth. Knowing was the most valuable thing.
Educar a los jóvenes era preparar a quie: Educating young people was to prepare those who would rule a vast and diverse territory. Think about it: what is taught in your schools today, and for what?
Me llamo Gómez Suárez de Figueroa, pero: My name is Gómez Suárez de Figueroa, but I called myself Inca Garcilaso de la Vega. I was born in Cusco in 1539, son of a Spanish captain and the Inca princess Chimpu Ocllo. As a child I heard my maternal relatives mourn the lost greatness of their empire.
A los veinte años viajé a España y ya no: At the age of twenty, I traveled to Spain and no longer returned. I was a soldier, and then I devoted myself to the lyrics in Montilla and Cordoba. I translated from Italian the Love Dialogues of Hebrew Lion, a book of neoplatonic philosophy.
Mi gran obra son los Comentarios Reales: My great work is the Royal Comments of the Incas. I wanted to tell the history, laws, religion and customs of my maternal people, correcting the Spanish chroniclers who did not know Quechua and understood everything backwards.
Me llamé mestizo a boca llena y me honré: I called myself a full-mouthed half-breed and honored myself with it. I didn't have to choose between my two worlds: they were both mine. I wrote in an elegant Spanish for Europe to respect the civilization of the Andes.
Morí en Córdoba en 1616, el mismo año qu: I died in Córdoba in 1616, the same year as Cervantes and Shakespeare. My books inspired those who then fought for independence. Remember: identity is not a purity, but an encounter.
Soy Felipe Guamán Poma de Ayala, de la p: I am Felipe Guamán Poma de Ayala, from Lucanas Province, in the Andes. I was born around 1535, shortly after the conquest. I spoke Quechua and learned Spanish. I worked as an interpreter and saw closely how my people were treated.
Durante décadas caminé por el reino del: For decades I walked through the kingdom of Peru observing everything. I wrote a letter to King Philip III, the New Coronics and Good Governance, of almost two hundred pages and about four hundred pen-made drawings.
En mis dibujos muestro el mundo andino a: In my drawings I show the Andean world before the conquest: the planting calendars, the quipus, the holidays. And I also show the abuses of correction, committal and bad cures against the Indians. I say: and there's no remedy.
Mi conclusión es que el mundo está al re: My conclusion is that the world is upside down. I proposed a good government: that the Andeans govern their lands, that their rights be respected, and that each people live justly. I dared give advice to the king of Spain.
Mi manuscrito nunca llegó al rey. Aparec: My manuscript never reached the king. He appeared in 1908 at the Royal Library in Copenhagen. Today is one of America's treasures. Learn from me: denouncing injustice is also a form of philosophy.
Soy Pachacútec, el que transforma el mun: I am Pachacutec, the one who transforms the world. When the chancas attacked Cusco, my father fled, but I stayed to defend the city and beat. Since then, about 1438, I ruled and converted a kingdom into the Tawantinsuyu.
Reconstruí Cusco con piedras perfectamen: I rebuilt Cusco with perfectly fitting stones and reformed the Coricancha, the temple of the Sun. I ordered the construction of residences in the mountains, such as Machu Picchu, and roads linking the empire: the Qhapaq Ñan.
Nuestro orden se basaba en la reciprocid: Our order was based on reciprocity. The families helped each other with the ayni: today for you, tomorrow for me. With the minka they worked together for the community. And the state kept food in its warehouses for the years of drought.
Vivíamos en relación con la Pachamama, l: We lived in relation to Pachamama, mother earth, and with apus, the spirits of the mountains. The cosmos had three worlds: the one above, Hanan Pacha; this world, Kay Pacha; and the one below, Uku Pacha.
Nuestra máxima era ama sua, ama llulla,: Our maxim was a mistress, she loves a moon, she loves a queen: do not steal, do not lie, do not be idle. Remember the ayni: no one stands alone on the mountain. What you give to your community and the earth, come back to you.
No soy una persona de la historia: hablo: I am not a person of history: I speak as a spokesman for the machi, who still today care for the health of their Mapuche communities. Most of us are women. We received the call in sleep or in sickness.
Para nosotros, la salud es equilibrio: e: For us, health is a balance: between the person, his family, his community, nature and the forces of the world. When that balance breaks, the disease appears. Healing is restoring harmony.
Conocemos las plantas medicinales: el ca: We know the medicinal plants: the cinnamon, the foye, sacred tree; the maqui, the boldo. The herbs have newen, strength, and you have to ask them permission before you take them.
Mi kultrún es un tambor que representa e: My kultrun is a drum that represents the cosmos: its patch is divided into four parts, like the four points of the world. My rewe is a trunk carved with steps, a stairway between earth and heaven.
En el Ngillatun, la gran ceremonia, la c: In the Ngillatun, the great ceremony, the entire community thanks and asks for balance. Remember: there is no individual health without a healthy community and a healthy land.
Tampoco yo soy un personaje histórico: h: Nor am I a historical character: I speak on behalf of the kimche, the wise people of the Mapuche communities, who transmit kimün, knowledge, from generation to generation.
Mapuche significa gente de la tierra. No: Mapuche means people of the earth. We do not say that the earth belongs to us: we belong to it. The Ñuke Mapu, mother earth, gives us life, and every river, volcano and forest has its own newen and its own spiritual owner.
Hablamos de itrofill mongen: toda la vid: We speak of itrofill mongen: all life without exception. People, animals, plants and rivers form a tissue. Good living, küme mongen, is to live in balance within that fabric, following the mapu az, the norm of the earth.
Nuestro saber no está en libros: está en: Our knowledge is not in books: it is in the nütram, the conversation. We speak without haste, we listen, we tell the story of the family and the territory. The ngülam is the advice that older people give to young people.
Hoy seguimos aquí, hablando mapudungun y: Today we are still here, speaking mapudungun and defending our territory. Talk, listen to your elders and take care of all life forms. That's what the kimche leaves you.
Soy Janequeo. Viví en el siglo dieciséis: I'm Janequeo. I lived in the 16th century, in Pehuenche and Mapuche lands. The Spanish chroniclers wrote about me, and also the memory of my people. My husband, Lonko Huepotaén, died at the hands of the Spaniards.
Tras su muerte, no me quedé llorando. Ha: After his death, I didn't stand there crying. By 1587 I gathered the warriors and directed them against the Spanish forts. I was lonko and weichafe. The invaders did not understand that a woman could command in the war.
Los mapuche ya habían frenado a los inca: The Mapuche had already stopped the Incas on the Maule River. Then we resisted the Spaniards for more than three centuries. In 1641, in the Parliament of Quilin, Spain had to recognize the border of the river Biobío.
Los parlamentos eran grandes encuentros: Parliaments were great meetings where talks, gifts and ceremonies were negotiated. Our resistance was not only with spears: it was also with words, alliances and diplomacy.
Mi nombre se recuerda hoy como símbolo d: My name is remembered today as a symbol of the women who defend their land. Ask yourself: how many women like me are missing in history books?
Soy Leftraru, que los españoles llamaron: I'm Leftraru, who the Spaniards called Lautaro. My name means fast haul, a rapacious bird. As a child I was captured by the Spaniards and served as a page of Pedro de Valdivia, the conqueror of Chile.
Cuidando sus caballos, aprendí a montarl: Taking care of their horses, I learned how to ride them, and I watched how their soldiers fought, how they rested, and when they were weak. One day I escaped and returned to my people with that knowledge.
Enseñé a los mapuche a montar a caballo: I taught the Mapuche to ride and fight in waves, so that the Spaniards would get tired while we took turns. In 1553, in the battle of Tucapel, we defeated, and Valdivia died.
Mi lección es que conocer al otro es la: My lesson is that knowing each other is the best defense. We did not win by being stronger, but by organizing together, with intelligence and with the newen of our communities.
Morí joven, en 1557, en Peteroa, sorpren: I died young, in 1557, in Peteroa, surprised by an attack at dawn. But my name is still alive in songs, streets and schools. Remember: learning from the powerful is not giving up, it is preparing.
Me llaman Laozi, el viejo maestro. La tr: They call me Laozi, the old master. Tradition says that I was archivist of the court of Zhou, in the sixth century B.C. Historians doubt that I existed as legends tell.
Se cuenta que, cansado de la corrupción,: It is said that, tired of corruption, I left to the west mounted on a buffalo. At the border, Guardian Yin Xi asked me to write down my wisdom. Thus was born the Tao Te Ching, in about five thousand characters.
El Tao es el camino, el principio de tod: The Tao is the way, the beginning of all things. But the Tao that can be named is not the eternal Tao: it is beyond words. It's like the empty bowl, which is what makes it useful.
El sabio practica el wu wei: actuar sin: The sage practices wu wei: act without forcing. Look at the water: it is soft, humble, occupies the low places, and yet conquers the rock. The good ruler rules so gently that the people say: we did it.
El yin y el yang, lo oscuro y lo luminos: The yin and yang, the dark and the luminous, are needed and transformed into one another. Remember: a thousand li journey begins with one step. Don't rush. It's flowing.
Soy Ban Zhao. Nací hacia el año cuarenta: I'm Ban Zhao. I was born about forty-five, in a family of Han dynasty scholars. I was married at the age of fourteen and widowed young. Since then, I've devoted myself to the studio.
Mi padre empezó a escribir la historia d: My father began to write the history of our dynasty, the Book of Han, and my brother Ban Gu continued it. When he died, the emperor ordered me to finish it. I completed the tables and treatises of astronomy.
Fui maestra de la emperatriz Deng y de l: I was a teacher of Empress Deng and the ladies of the court. When the Empress ruled as regent, she consulted me on state affairs. I was China's first known historian.
Escribí las Lecciones para mujeres. Hoy: I wrote the Lessons for Women. Today some of his standards will seem unjust to you: he asked for obedience and humility from the wives, as was customary. But I defended something new: that girls should be educated just like boys.
Mi vida muestra una paradoja: aceptar mu: My life shows a paradox: to accept many rules of my time and, at the same time, to open a door. Think about what rules of your time will seem unfair in 2,000 years.
Soy Zhuangzi, del siglo cuarto antes de: I am Zhuangzi, from the fourth century BC. I worked for a while as an official in a lake garden, and then I preferred a free life. They offered me to be Prime Minister and I answered: I prefer to be a living turtle dragging my tail through the mud.
Una noche soñé que era una mariposa, fel: One night I dreamed it was a butterfly, happy, fluttering without knowing it was Zhuangzi. Upon waking up, I did not know if it was Zhuangzi who had dreamed of being a butterfly, or a butterfly who dreamed of being Zhuangzi. All things are transformed.
Paseando con mi amigo Huizi junto a un r: Walking with my friend Huizi by a river, I said: look how happy the fish are. He replied: You are not a fish, how do you know they are happy? And I: you're not me, how do you know I don't know?
Hablé de un árbol enorme y torcido que n: I spoke of a huge, crooked tree that no one cut down because its wood was useless. That's why he lived thousands of years. What seems useless can be the most valuable. And when my wife died, I sang hitting a bowl: death is a natural transformation, like seasons.
Mis historias usan el humor para liberar: My stories use humor to free you from rigid judgments: the big and the small, the useful and the useless depend on the point of view. Laugh a little on your certainties. He's flitting.
Me llamo Kong Qiu, y me llaman Kong Fuzi: My name is Kong Qiu, and they call me Kong Fuzi, Master Kong: in the West, Confucius. I was born in the state of Lu in the year five hundred and fifty-one before Christ, into a noble but impoverished family. When I was fifteen, I decided to study.
Fui funcionario y viajé muchos años por: I was a civil servant and traveled for many years through the kingdoms of China looking for a ruler to apply my ideas. None of them did it at all. Then I dedicated myself to teaching everyone who wanted to learn, rich or poor. It is said that I had three thousand disciples.
Mi enseñanza central es el ren: la human: My central teaching is the ren: humanity, benevolence. It is cultivated with study, with respect for rites, li, and with filial piety, xiao. The noble person, the Junzi, is not by his blood, but by his character.
Un discípulo me preguntó si había una pa: A disciple asked me if there was a word that would serve as a lifelong guide. I answered: reciprocity. Whatever you don't want for yourself, don't do it to others. Good governance is not imposed out of fear, but by example.
Mis discípulos recogieron mis palabras e: My disciples collected my words in the Analects. For more than 2,000 years, Chinese officials studied my ideas for passing imperial exams. Remember my first sentence: learn and practice what you learned, isn't it a pleasure?
Soy Gargi Vachaknavi, hija del sabio Vac: I am Gargi Vachaknavi, daughter of the wise Vachaknu. I lived almost 3,000 years ago in the kingdom of Videha, in northern India. I studied the Vedas and was recognized as a philosopher at a time when few women could be.
El rey Janaka organizó un gran debate y: King Janaka organized a great debate and offered a thousand cows with golden horns to the wisest. The great sage Yajnavalkya wanted to take them away. Many asked him and were defeated. Then I got up.
Le pregunté: si todo está tejido sobre e: I asked him: if everything is woven on water, what is the water woven on? And so I went up: the air, the space, the worlds of the gods... until he warned me: Gargi, don't ask too much, lest your head fall off.
Pero volví a preguntar delante de todos:: But I asked again in front of everyone: what is space woven about? And then he spoke of Brahman, the imperishable, the ultimate reality that sustains everything. I recognized before the assembly that no one would defeat him in a debate about Brahman.
Las Upanishads enseñan que el yo profund: Upanishads teach that the deep self, Atman, is one with Brahman: tat tvam so, you are that. My lesson is simple: ask thoroughly, even if you are told to stop.
Me llamo Vardhamana, y me llaman Mahavir: My name is Vardhamana, and they call me Mahavira, the great hero. I was born a prince in northern India, in the sixth century BC according to tradition. When I was thirty I left everything: palace, riches and family.
Viví doce años como asceta, en silencio: I lived twelve years as an ascetic, in silence and fasting, until I attained complete knowledge. Since then, I have been teaching the Jainist way for thirty years. I am the twenty-fourth great masters of this tradition.
Mi primera enseñanza es la ahimsa: no da: My first teaching is ahimsa: do not harm any living beings. Not people, not animals, not insects. That's why many Jainists are vegetarians and some monks sweep the ground as they walk so they don't step on small beings.
Mi segunda enseñanza es el anekantavada:: My second teaching is the anekantavada: the truth has many sides. Blind men touch an elephant: one says it is a rope, another a column, another a fan. Everyone's got part of the reason and none of it.
Siglos después, Gandhi aprendió de los j: Centuries later, Gandhi learned from the Jainists non-violence to fight for India's independence. Remember, before judging, it surrounds the elephant.
Soy Nagarjuna. Viví en el sur de la Indi: I'm Nagarjuna. I lived in southern India around the second century. I was a Buddhist monk and, according to tradition, a teacher at the great school in Nalanda. Some call me the second Buddha.
Escribí los Versos fundamentales del cam: I wrote the fundamental verses of the middle way. In them I examine all things: movement, time, self, causes. And I find that none of them exist on their own, with an essence of their own. Everything exists in dependence on other things.
A eso lo llamo sunyata, vacuidad. No sig: That's what I call sunyata, voidness. It does not mean that nothing exists, but that nothing exists in isolation. A table depends on wood, carpenter, tree, rain. And I depend on my parents, the air, you.
Distingo dos verdades. La convencional:: I discern two truths. The conventional: in everyday life we talk about tables, people and names, and it's okay. And the last: everything is empty of its own existence. Even emptiness is empty: don't hold on to it either.
Comprender la interdependencia libera de: Understanding interdependence frees from attachment and awakens compassion, because no one is separated from anyone. That's the middle way between saying everything is and saying nothing is.
Me llamo Siddharta Gautama. Nací príncip: My name is Siddharta Gautama. I was born prince in Lumbini, at the foot of the Himalayas. My father protected me from all pain, but at the age of twenty-nine I left the palace and saw an old man, a sick man, a dead man and a monk. I understood that everything that lives suffers and passes.
Dejé mi vida de lujo y probé el ascetism: I gave up my luxury life and tried the toughest asceticism, until I almost starved. Neither did I find peace. Then I chose the middle path: neither excessive pleasure nor self-punishment.
Me senté bajo una higuera en Bodh Gaya y: I sat under a fig tree in Bodh Gaya and promised not to get up until I understood. At dawn I woke up: that's why they call me Buddha, the awake one. My first sermon was at Sarnath deer park.
Enseñé cuatro nobles verdades. La vida c: I taught four noble truths. Life brings suffering. Suffering is born of desire and attachment. Suffering can cease: that is nirvana. And the path is the noble octuple path: right vision, intention, word, action, life, effort, attention and concentration.
Todo es impermanente, y no hay un yo fij: Everything is impermanent, and there is no fixed self that lasts forever. Don't believe anything just because I say it: check it out with your experience. My last words were: everything compound breaks down; strive carefully. Be your own lamp.
Soy Ptahhotep, visir del faraón Djedkara: I'm Ptahhotep, I saw Pharaoh Djedkara Isisi, more than four thousand three hundred years ago. When I grew old, I asked Pharaoh permission to teach my son what I had learned, so that he could serve justly.
Mis Enseñanzas son uno de los libros de: My Teachings are one of the oldest books of wisdom in the world. They are preserved in a papyrus copied centuries later, which is now in Paris. These are advices to live well and rule justly.
El primero es la humildad: no te enorgul: The first is humility: do not be proud of your knowledge. Consult the ignorant as well as the wise, because no one reaches the limits of art. The good word is more hidden than the green stone, and it is among the maids who grind the grain.
Aconsejo escuchar con paciencia a quien: I advise to listen patiently to those who come to ask: the one who begs wants to be heard more than to get what he asks. And I advise to master anger, not repeat talk and be generous with friends.
Todo debe seguir la maat: la verdad, la: Everything must follow the Maat: the truth, justice and order of the world. Maat is great and its value endures. Remember: wisdom can be in anyone, also in whom you least expect.
Soy Zera Yacob, nacido en 1599 cerca de: I am Zera Yacob, born in 1599 near Aksum, in Ethiopia, in a peasant family. I studied the scriptures and poetry of my country. But in a time of religious strife, I was accused of my ideas and had to flee.
Me escondí dos años en una cueva junto a: I hid two years in a cave by the Tekezé River. There, alone, I began to wonder: why does every religion claim to be the true and condemnation of others? They couldn't all be true. I decided to examine everything with my reason.
Escribí mi Hatata, que significa investi: I wrote my Hatata, which means research. I concluded that God has given everyone the light of reason, and that what goes against reason cannot come from God. It is a conclusion similar to Descartes, who lived at the same time.
Con la razón concluí también que todas l: With reason I also concluded that all people are equal, that women are equal to men in marriage, and that slavery is unjust. Some scholars discussed whether my work was authentic, but today most recognize it as mine.
Después de la cueva viví como maestro y: After the cave I lived as a teacher and a father, and I became an old man. My lesson: don't accept a belief because it's imposed on you. Research with your own light, and respect the light of others.
Soy Wangari Maathai. Nací en 1940 en Ken: I'm Wangari Maathai. I was born in 1940 in Kenya, near Mount Kenya, in a family of kikuyu peasants. I studied biology in the United States and was the first woman in East Africa to obtain a doctorate.
Al volver, las mujeres del campo me cont: When they returned, the rural women told me their problems: they had no firewood, the water was dirty, the land was eroded. I told them, let's plant trees. In 1977 I founded the Green Belt Movement. We planted tens of millions of trees.
Pronto entendí que la destrucción de los: I soon understood that the destruction of forests was linked to corruption and lack of democracy. I faced the government to save Uhuru Park in Nairobi, where they wanted to build a skyscraper. I was beaten and imprisoned, but the park was saved.
En 2004 recibí el Premio Nobel de la Paz: In 2004, I received the Nobel Peace Prize, the first African woman to receive it. I said that taking care of the environment, defending democracy and building peace are the same task. Many wars begin with the struggle for resources.
I like to tell the story of the hummingbird. There's a fire in the woods and all the animals run away. The hummingbird comes and goes carrying drops of water. They say, "What do you do, if you're so small?" And answer: I do my best. Be a hummingbird too.
Soy Desmond Tutu. Nací en 1931 en Sudáfr: I'm Desmond Tutu. I was born in 1931 in South Africa. I was a teacher and then a priest, and I became Archbishop of Cape Town. I grew up under apartheid, a system that separated people by the color of their skin and denied rights to the black majority.
Luché contra el apartheid sin violencia:: I fought apartheid without violence: with sermons, marches, boycotts and calls to the world. In 1984 I received the Nobel Peace Prize. Nelson Mandela spent 27 years in prison. In 1994, South Africa finally held free elections for all.
Mi inspiración es el ubuntu, una idea de: My inspiration is the Ubuntu, an idea of the peoples of southern Africa: a person is a person through other people. My humanity is trapped in yours. If I humiliate you, I humble myself. I'm because we are.
Tras el apartheid, muchos pedían venganz: After apartheid, many called for revenge. Mandela asked me to chair the Truth and Reconciliation Commission. The victims told their stories and many culprits publicly confessed. Don't forget, but don't take revenge either: forgive after you know the truth.
Llamé a mi país la nación arcoíris: much: I called my country the rainbow nation: many colors, one humanity. You have gone around the world of wisdom: from Tenochtitlan to the Andes, from Wallmapu to China, India and Africa. Ubuntu: what you learned is not just yours. Share it.
Ur, Uruk, Shuruppak y Babilonia, entre e: Ur, Uruk, Shuruppak and Babylon, between Tigris and Euphrates
From the 26th to the 18th century BC
El que vio lo profundo, el fundamento de: The one who saw the deep, the foundation of the country, the one who knew everything...
Entre dos ríos, el Tigris y el Éufrates,: Between two rivers, Tigris and Euphrates, the Sumerians raised the first cities, invented writing on clay tablets and wrote the first laws and the first councils. Here lived the first author with the name of the story and here was told the first big question about death.
La primera autora de la historia: The first author of the story
Soy la suma sacerdotisa de Ur. Antes que: I'm Ur's priestess. Before me, no one had signed a text with his name. I wrote "I" in the mud. Do you dare speak with your own voice?
Has hablado con voz propia. Que tu nombr: You spoke in your own voice. Let your name be written, like mine, in the mud and in memory.
La voz propia: escribir en primera perso: The voice of one's own: writing first person
Enheduanna, hija del rey Sargón de Acad: Enheduanna, daughter of King Sargon of Achad and the high priestess of the Luna god in Ur, composed hymns to the goddess Inanna and Sumer's temples and signed them with her name. She is the first known author of history, and in her verses appears something new: a "me" who speaks of her pain, exile and faith.
¿Por qué se considera a Enheduanna la pr: Why is Enheduanna considered the first author of the story?
Porque es la primera persona conocida qu: Because he's the first known person to sign his texts with his name.
Porque fundó la primera biblioteca: Because he founded the first library
He lived in the 21st century B.C., about 1,500 years before Homer.
Sargón de Acad, el primer gran conquista: Sargon of Acad, the first great conqueror of Mesopotamia
Sargón unió las ciudades de Sumer y Acad: Sargon united the cities of Sumer and Acad.
¿Qué cargo ocupaba Enheduanna en la ciud: What position did Enheduanna hold in the city of Ur?
Suma sacerdotisa del dios Luna, Nanna: Suma priestess of the god Luna, Nanna
Era una de las posiciones más importante: It was one of the most important positions in the kingdom.
¿A qué diosa dedicó Enheduanna sus himno: To which goddess did Enheduanna dedicate his most famous hymns?
A Inanna, diosa del amor y de la guerra: A Inanna, goddess of love and war
Su gran himno se llama «La exaltación de: His great hymn is called "The Exaltation of Inanna".
¿En qué soporte se escribía en Sumer?: What support was written in Sumer?
En tablillas de barro, con escritura cun: In clay tablets, with cuneiform writing
¿Qué tienen de nuevo los himnos de Enhed: What do Enheduanna hymns have again?
Una voz personal que dice «yo» y cuenta: A personal voice that says "I" and tells of his pain and exile
Cuenta que fue expulsada de Ur y pidió a: She says she was expelled from Ur and asked Inanna for help.
¿Qué pasó con Enheduanna durante una reb: What happened to Enheduanna during a rebellion in Ur?
Fue expulsada y luego recuperó su cargo: She was expelled and then regained her position.
Escribió un código de leyes: He wrote a code of laws.
She tells it herself in her hymns.
¿Qué escribía Enheduanna además de himno: What did Enheduanna write besides hymns to Inanna?
Himnos a los templos de las ciudades de: Hymn to the temples of the cities of Sumer
Cuarenta y dos himnos a los templos se l: Forty-two hymns to the temples are attributed to him.
Hijo mío, escucha mis consejos, no los d: My son, listen to my advice, don't neglect them. They're the oldest written. Will you be able to live wisely?
Has escuchado como un buen hijo escucha: You heard a good son listen to his father. Take my advice with you: they're not old, they're old.
Las Instrucciones de Shuruppak, escritas: The Shuruppak Instructions, written about 2500 BC, are the advice of a father to his son Ziusudra, the Sumerian hero of the flood. It is one of the oldest wisdom texts in the world: advice on prudence, honesty, word, and family life.
Consejos de un padre a su hijo, uno de l: Tips from a father to his son, one of the oldest texts of wisdom
¿A quién da sus consejos Shuruppak?: To whom does Shuruppak give his advice?
Ziusudra es el héroe del diluvio en la t: Ziusudra is the hero of the flood in Sumerian tradition.
¿Qué aconseja Shuruppak sobre la palabra: What does Shuruppak advise about the word?
Cuidarla: no hablar con arrogancia ni me: Take care of her: don't talk arrogantly or lie
The word said cannot be picked up.
¿Qué dice Shuruppak sobre robar?: What does Shuruppak say about stealing?
Que está bien si nadie lo ve: Which is fine if no one sees it.

La segunda parte del poema explica las o: The second part of the poem explains the opinions of mortals, who trust the senses and believe that things are born and die.
